messages:
Maria (eng-platform): quick heads-up: I ran into a surprising routing case while testing header-based model selection. Sent `x-redwood-model: gpt-4r-v2` but the request ended up on the tenant-default alias `gpt-4r-v1`.
Omar (eng-api): can you paste the route matcher and a repro curl?
Maria (eng-platform): Route matcher is straightforward, set in Console -> API routes. Matchers: path prefix `/v1/`, header `x-redwood-model` present. Action: `model_alias: gpt-4r-v2`. Repro: `curl -H "x-redwood-model: gpt-4r-v2" https://api.redwood.mock/v1/generate`
Liam (eng-runtime): Do you have any tenant-level header injection/policies? We sometimes rewrite headers at the proxy for legacy clients.
Maria (eng-platform): Turns out yes: tenant policy injects `x-redwood-model` for some clients. In my test both client and tenant headers were present; tenant value was `gpt-4r-v1`.
Sara (devex): FYI we canonicalize to tenant header when both present. Historically done for compliance and to enforce org-level pinning.
Maria (eng-platform): That behavior surprised me. For obvious reasons customers expect an explicit client pin to win when they set a header per-request.
Omar (eng-api): Seems like three things to resolve: clarify precedence rules, optionally allow routes to accept client overrides, and surface routing traces in responses for debugging.
Kevin (product): +1. UX should show why a model was chosen (policy trace) and allow a per-route toggle `client_can_override` with a tooltip explaining performance tradeoffs.
Liam (eng-runtime): Implementation note: runtime currently resolves model in fixed order: route action -> tenant override -> client header. Changing precedence is doable but watch cache keys and batching partitions. Per-request client pins will fragment batch groups.
Maria (eng-platform): Proposal for matcher schema change: add `override_priority` enum in matcher metadata with values `tenant`, `route`, `client`. Default remains `tenant` for safety. Example:

```
{
  "match": [{"path_prefix": "/v1/"}, {"header": {"name": "x-redwood-model", "present": true}}],
  "action": {"model_alias": "gpt-4r-v2"},
  "meta": {"override_priority": "client"}
}
```

When set to `client`, a client-supplied `x-redwood-model` should take precedence over the tenant-injected header.
Sara (devex): Also propose adding compatibility predicates to alias metadata: `min_ctx`, `requires_kv_cache`, `quantized_ok`. Router should check compatibility before honoring a pin.
Omar (eng-api): Good call. If a pinned alias is incompatible with request parameters we should either reject with 4xx and explain, or auto-fallback to the nearest-compatible model and include `routing_trace` explaining why.
Maria (eng-platform): Example response when pin incompatible:

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "error": "Pinned model gpt-4r-v2 incompatible with request: requires_kv_cache=true",
  "selected_model": "gpt-4r-v1",
  "routing_trace": ["route_action: alias=gpt-4r-v2", "compat_check: failed requires_kv_cache"]
}
```

Alternatively `selected_model` could be omitted when we choose to reject.
Liam (eng-runtime): We should also emit response header `x-redwood-selected-model: gpt-4r-v1` for normal flows and `x-redwood-routing-trace: ...` when `?debug_routing=true`. Telemetry fields: `routing.priority`, `routing.reason`, `routing.fallback_source` are useful for analytics and alerts.
Kevin (product): For Console: show last-24h breakdown per-route of requests that were pinned vs auto-selected, count of overrides applied, and top fallback reasons. Add a lightweight "why this model" flyout on each request sample.
Maria (eng-platform): UX caveat: allow teams to opt into `client` priority on a per-route basis. Default stays conservative. I'll draft a short RFC and a prototype API param `override_priority` for the matcher and a `client_can_override` toggle in Console.
Sara (devex): I'll mock the Console toggle and a routing trace panel that shows the evaluated policies and the final selected alias. Include the compatibility checks and a clear call-to-action when an alias is incompatible (unpin, change route, or enable tenant feature).
Omar (eng-api): API contract changes: responses include `x-redwood-selected-model`, and `?debug_routing=true` returns `routing_trace` in JSON. Also, add an event `routing.override_applied` to our telemetry stream with tags: `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `requested_alias`, `selected_alias`, `priority`.
Liam (eng-runtime): Dev note: changing priority semantics requires updating cache key computation and the batching router. We'll add recommendation text in Console: "If you expect high QPS, prefer alias families or tenant-level pins to avoid batch fragmentation." Also flag routes that would cause high fragmentation.
Maria (eng-platform): Action items: I'll produce RFC + tests, Liam will scope batching/cache impacts, Sara will deliver console mocks, Kevin will write product copy for the toggle and the routing trace. Omar will update API docs and add response headers. I'll share the prototype PR link here when ready.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: feature/routing-override -> staging at 2026-04-01T03:00Z :rocket:

Liam (eng-runtime): assigning follow-ups in the ticket. thanks for catching this, Maria.
Maria (eng-platform): Thanks all. Quick manual test for folks who want to try: `curl -H "x-redwood-model:gpt-4r-v2" -H "x-tenant-model:gpt-4r-v1" https://staging.api.redwood.mock/v1/generate -i` and inspect `x-redwood-selected-model` header.
Sara (devex): :party:
